page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a frequency of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 2 vCPUs, which are mapped from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, the server achieved a single-core CPU score of 1161.28 and a multi-core score of 2371.48, both falling in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 187.49 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds drop to 22.38 GB/sec and 19.14 GB/sec respectively. Geekbench multi-core and software compilation tests also rank in the bottom 10%, reflecting the constraints of the burstable CPU allocation model.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and lower-tier benchmark results, the ecs.t6-c1m4.large is designed as a budget-friendly option for workloads with low baseline CPU utilization that experience occasional spikes. It offers a cost-effective entry point for lightweight applications, development and testing environments, low-traffic web servers, and basic microservices. It is not suitable for sustained high-compute tasks, database operations, or memory-intensive workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is a burstable, KVM-based virtual machine designed for budget-conscious workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, it features 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM. The instance does not include local storage or baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks, including stress-ng and Geekbench, consistently place this instance in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware, reflecting its burstable CPU allocation. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for low-utilization tasks but exhibits significant performance tradeoffs under sustained loads. With 4.0 GB of RAM per core, it supports basic memory requirements but is constrained by its shared-core architecture and lack of dedicated network throughput. This instance is best suited for lightweight applications, development environments, and low-traffic web servers.
